data.title: Keylogging Capability
data.summary: The sample installs a keyboard hook or polls key state to record keystrokes to a local buffer or file for later exfiltration, independent of which application has focus.
data.description:
The two common mechanisms are a low-level keyboard hook (SetWindowsHookEx with
WH_KEYBOARD_LL) and polling GetAsyncKeyState in a tight loop; the former sees every
keystroke system-wide through a single callback, the latter requires no hook installation
at all and is correspondingly harder for hook-enumeration tools to find. Captured output is
typically buffered locally and exfiltrated in batches rather than streamed live, to reduce
network noise.
data.recommendation:
* Check for both hook-based (SetWindowsHookEx) and polling-based (GetAsyncKeyState loop) capture; the second leaves no hook-chain artefact to enumerate.
* Locate and recover the local capture buffer or log file before it is next exfiltrated and cleared.
* Rotate credentials typed on the affected host since the estimated infection window, prioritising anything typed while the hook was confirmed active.
data.short_recommendation: Check for polling-based capture in addition to hook-based, and recover the local log before exfiltration.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Buffered captured keystrokes to a local file and exfiltrated the file in batches over the existing C2 channel.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Installed a WH_KEYBOARD_LL hook capturing system-wide keystrokes independent of window focus.
